items.excerpt: Opinion by UK Phones Editor Tom Pritchard arguing that smartphones over-index on AI marketing while core hardware qualities stagnate — a pointed counter-take landing days before Samsung's AI-heavy Galaxy Unpacked (July 22, Galaxy Z Fold 8 / Galaxy Glasses). Newest item in the pool (published 05 Jul). Body is truncated behind Tom's Guide markup; writer should re-fetch or quote from headline/dek.

MemoMind One — XGIMI's new AI-hardware brand — blasts past $500K (~$586K) on Kickstarter for camera-less smart glasses with dual 2,000-nit green micro-LED displays, on-device AI assistant, 26+ language real-time translation, note-taking, navigation and teleprompter, from $400 (Memo+ subscription $20/mo planned); ships later this summer. DUPE GROUP memomind-one: pairs with TechRadar's 48h review — pick one.

48-hour hands-on with the MemoMind One XR glasses: slow AI responses, no camera and disappointing audio leave the reviewer unable to recommend them over rival smart glasses — the skeptical counterweight to the $500K+ Kickstarter hype. DUPE GROUP memomind-one: pairs with Road to VR's crowdfunding story — pick one.

Minix ER939-AI mini PC packs AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 (16 cores / 32 threads, up to 5.1 GHz) with 128GB RAM, metal feet and a vegan-leather handle — a workstation-in-a-box built for running AI workloads entirely locally, no cloud dependence. Distinct product from the already-published GMKtec Ryzen AI Max 395 tower.

Android chief Sameer Samat explains 'Android Halo' — a persistent status-bar slot where Gemini or third-party agents surface updates and questions from long-running background tasks — plus how Gemini in Android Automotive will use front-facing car cameras to answer questions about road conditions. Device angle: phones and cars as agent hardware surfaces (Android 17).

Rogbid VisionPro smart glasses launch at $119.99 with a 13 MP Sony IMX386 camera, dual-chip AI processor, real-time object/landmark recognition, on-the-fly text and conversation translation, photochromic lenses and 10-12h battery — an AI-glasses entry point at less than a third of Ray-Ban Meta's price.

Analysis: AR glasses like Snap's $2,200 Specs still have a massive size problem — cramming wearable-computer guts into eyewear keeps them bulky and socially awkward, an engineering tension that may be unsolvable near-term. CAUTION: piece is design/size-focused with no explicit AI hook; weakest relevance in pool — use only if curator accepts the AR-race framing around AI-glasses contenders.

Google's latest Gemini for Home update brings big improvements to the voice assistant and camera intelligence on Google Home/Nest speakers and displays — smarter multi-step commands and camera-feed understanding as Gemini replaces Assistant across home hardware. NOTE: aging (06-23) and adjacent to the already-published Google Home Speaker review — confirm distinct angle before use.

Hands-on with Meta's new AI Glasses trio — Fury and Adventurer ($299) plus the Kylie Jenner 'Starfire' edition ($399): 26 style/material combos, adjustable nose pads and hinges, launching alongside the Muse Spark AI update with dynamic photos and pedestrian navigation. NOTE: overlaps the already-published Meta Fury review (Gizmodo) — the lineup/strategy angle is what's new; aging (06-23).

Karissa Bell reviews Ray-Ban Meta Optics ($499+), the prescription-first line of Meta's Gen 2 AI glasses: Blayzer and Scriber frames with swappable nosepads, adjustable temple tips, customizable action button, 8h+ battery and progressive/transition lens support — the most comfortable way to get Meta AI in everyday prescription eyewear. NOTE: oldest item in pool (06-22, ~318h) — near the 336h edge.
